newsitem.title: USA: Noxso agrees to convert to Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Noxso agrees to convert to Chapter 11.

text.p: Noxso Corp said Wednesday it will consent to convert its bankruptcy proceeding to a Chapter 11 reorganization.

The company said it will consent to the jurisdiction of the U.S. bankruptcy court for the Eastern district of Tennessee, pursuant to the involuntary petition in bankruptcy filed by Olin Corp and two other creditors.
Noxso's action will not affect its ability to maintain a pending lawsuit against Olin, Noxso said.
Under Chapter 11, Noxso has a minimum of 120 days to submit a plan of reorganization to the bankruptcy court.

In a written statement, Noxso President and Chief Executive Officer Edwin J. Kilpela said, "We are presently reviewing third-party expressions of interest either to purchase the plant we have constructed on Olin's property, or to buy the stream of income under Noxso's supply agreement with Olin."

"In addition, the company has entered negotiations for a new host site agreement to commercially demonstrate the Noxso process," Kilpela said. "We believe that operating under the protection of the bankruptcy court affords Noxso the best opportunity to move forward with these business activities."
